Orthopedics · published research

Osteoporosis

The eight-person low-intensity PBM study found increased density at two sites but not others; two publications from one high-intensity laser cohort report no density gain with laser alone and a modest lumbar-density change when paired with exercise.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

The eight-person low-intensity PBM study found increased density at two sites but not others; two publications from one high-intensity laser cohort report no density gain with laser alone and a modest lumbar-density change when paired with exercise.

Summary of the Evidence

The Bone > Osteoporosis category contains 24 titles, with one related osteoporotic stem-cell experiment mapped from a linked category, for 25 publications in this review. The records include four human publications, 20 rat studies, and one in-vitro study. Two human publications report the same 100-person high-intensity laser trial cohort and must not be counted as separate trials.

Human and clinical evidence

A small quasi-experimental study in eight people with complete spinal-cord injury and osteoporosis used conventional near-infrared PBM. Bone density increased at the proximal femur and forearm, while distal femur and tibia density and bone markers did not change (Mohammadzadeh et al. 2024). Two papers by Alayat and colleagues describe follow-up from one 100-person HILT-plus-exercise randomized cohort. HILT alone did not increase bone density; the HILT-plus-exercise arm showed a modest lumbar-density change compared with exercise, with a later report describing persistence at one year (Alayat et al. 2017 Alayat et al. 2018). HILT is a high-intensity modality and is distinguished from low-intensity PBM. A separate comparison in women used both high-intensity and lower-level laser and is not a clean estimate of one PBM protocol.

Animal evidence

Twenty rat studies examine ovariectomy, osteopenia, osteoporosis, or related bone models. Findings include changes in density or bone structure, but models and irradiation schedules vary and do not establish patient outcomes (Shokri et al. 2023).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

One linked publication studies osteoporotic bone-marrow mesenchymal stem cells in vitro. No standalone ex-vivo study was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The eight-person clinical PBM study used an 830-nm near-infrared laser at 200 mW three times weekly for eight weeks, with reported energy density adjusted to target depth. The Alayat trial used 1064-nm high-intensity laser. Another comparison includes 633-nm red and 904-nm near-infrared low-level laser alongside HILT. The different modalities and anatomic measurements should not be combined as one treatment effect.

Interpretation

Human evidence remains limited, especially for conventional PBM. Rat and cell findings are more numerous but do not establish a clinical effect on osteoporosis.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for low-intensity PBM improving bone density in osteoporosis Low for a small lumbar-density change when high-intensity laser is combined with exercise
Publications and records25 unique titles (24 exact Bone > Osteoporosis titles plus 1 linked osteoporotic stem-cell in-vitro title)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Four human publications include a very small conventional-PBM study and two reports from the same 100-person high-intensity laser trial, alongside another comparison study. Most records are rat experiments. The settings, populations, and density sites differ, and publications from one cohort must not be counted as separate trials. Independent PBM trials with controlled density follow-up are needed.
